name: Buff-Yellow
lede: Buff-Yellow is a light orange-yellow carried in Ridgway's standards since 1886.

sections.title: An 1886 record
sections.body: Our library's earliest citation for Buff-Yellow is Ridgway's 1886 Nomenclature of Colors, carried over into his fuller 1912 standards at plate IV, hue 19; the 1955 ISCC-NBS system classes a close match as a light yellow [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[mustard-yellow]], [[ochre-yellow]], [[pale-orange-yellow]] and [[buff-orange]], at 3, 3.3, 3, 3.5 and 4.5 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Buff-Yellow in 341 of 23,781 paintings (1.43 percent), as photographed [2]. It peaks in the 1300s, in 5 of 251 paintings, at 1.5 times the archive's overall rate, and is over-represented in paintings from Japan (2.3 times expected) and the Mughal school especially (5.1 times) [2]. It most often plays an accent, and keeps company with Dusty Marigold and Pinchbeck Brown more than chance [2]. The earliest dated match, a 1326 work by Simone Martini, still comes 560 years before the 1886 record, which the archive's thin early coverage explains, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2].
